## SESSION 1 — Tooling and review baseline (established, still binding)

Keith is running a multi-agent coding pipeline for COSMOS2 + cDeck. Standing decisions from this session:

- Deterministic checks (Ruff, Pyright, pytest, Bandit, Semgrep) are the required gate BEFORE any AI review layer. AI review sits after CI is green, not instead of it.
- AI reviewers must produce citation-bound findings only: exact file, exact line/range, reproducible reason. No finding without evidence. This mirrors and extends the existing "a claim is not evidence" rule already in CSM_prompt-2.md.
- Every AI finding must be tagged blocking / important / suggestion, with a proposed test where applicable.
- Do not let repeated AI review become circular consensus — convergence between independently-run cheap models is signal; it is not proof by itself.
- CI pipeline shape (GitHub Actions): checkout -> setup Python -> install deps -> ruff format --check -> ruff check -> pyright -> pytest with coverage -> bandit -> semgrep. Target the actual package directory, never scan .venv or vendored code.

## SESSION 2 — Parallel agent architecture and 10-hour cDeck sprint (established, still binding)

- Fan-out / fan-in model: many proposers work in parallel; exactly one path (CCr, holding CCR.lease) disposes into the live tree. Constrained by existing P9 (orch!=execute) / P10 (propose/dispose) rules.
- Named crew routing (per CSM_prompt-2.md, reaffirmed):
  - GF38 (Vertex gemini-3.8-flash) = quality farm, UI/pane correctness, ALSO top of the coding escalation ladder (Terra removed, see below).
  - Luna Flex (openai/gpt-5.6-luna, openai/flex pin, allow_fallbacks false) = default cheap/routine coding tier.
  - GLM-5.3 Flash + Ling 3.0 Flash = cheap twins, ALWAYS dispatched as a pair on the same coding job for cross-check. Convergence = fast-track. Divergence = escalate, do not coin-flip.
  - Terra (openai/gpt-5.6-terra, --seat terra) = REMOVED from coding escalation. Do not route coding jobs to Terra. Terra IS permitted for REVIEW jobs (tie-breaker role, see Section 3) — a different role, not a contradiction.
- Coding escalation ladder (no Terra):
  1. Luna or GLM+Ling pair attempt.
  2. If twins disagree OR Luna fails local gate twice -> GF38.
  3. If GF38 fails local gate twice on hard-Python/concurrency -> STOP. Package as a design question, hold for Opus 5 or the review pipeline. Do not keep cycling cheap tiers.
  4. Never auto-retry a failed hard-Python coding job more than twice.
- Local deterministic gate daemon: watches work_orders/ccr/CREW/OUT/, applies each candidate diff to a SCRATCH checkout (never the live tree), runs ruff/pyright/pytest, writes a .gate.json verdict. Only "pass": true candidates reach Grok 4.6 aggregation.
- P11 prefix discipline is absolute: this preload (Sections 1+2) must be BYTE-IDENTICAL across every call in this package. No timestamps, job IDs, wave numbers, or status text inside Sections 1-2 — all of that goes in the per-call ITEM (Section 4) only. Verify cached_tokens is nonzero on the second and later calls to each seat; if zero, STOP and diff actual bytes sent before continuing.
- Opus 5 (Claude Pro, weekly-quota-metered, NOT pay-per-token) is reserved for ONE deep adjudication pass, AFTER the Day 2 verification loop below completes, reviewing anything touching cosmos_pool.py, cosmos_run.py, cosmos_ledger.py, fencing tokens, or src-tauri/api_request race conditions. Opus adjudicates a mature, already-verified diff — it does not do first-pass discovery. Opus quota resets Thursday; this package's Opus call (if triggered) MUST be the only Opus job before that reset.

## SESSION 3 — Cost-optimized review layer, tabs/feature completion (established, still binding)

- Review model roster for this package (OpenRouter): GPT-5.6 Sol ($5/M in, $30/M out), Claude Fable 5.1 ($10/M in, $50/M out, cache reads $0.25/M), GPT-5.6 Terra ($2/M in, $12/M out) as cheap tie-breaker only. Two DIFFERENT model families reviewing the same material is the actual point of running two reviews. Do not substitute convenience for this requirement.

## SESSION 4 (CURRENT) — Two-day budget, review-fix-verify structure (this package)

- Total budget for this package: $20 OpenRouter credit, spread across 2 days. Modeled actual cost is approximately $5.71 for the full structure below — the remaining ~$14 is a DELIBERATE CONTINGENCY RESERVE, not a target to spend. Do not add extra review passes, extra models, or broader scope just because budget remains. Only spend the reserve if a specific triggering condition in Section 3 fires (disagreement between reviewers, an unexpectedly severe finding, or a genuine need to re-run a step that failed).
- Structure: Day 1 = two independent reviews of current state + tabs deep dive + blueprint draft + independent blueprint critique. Between Day 1 and Day 2 = approved blueprint items become normal CREW/OUT coding jobs through the EXISTING crew pipeline (Luna/GLM+Ling/GF38), gated and disposed exactly as every other coding job this sprint — NO shortcut, NO exception, regardless of how the blueprint was produced. Day 2 = independent verification of the POST-FIX state (not the pre-fix state already reviewed on Day 1), using the same two-reviewer-model discipline, followed by the single reserved Opus 5 pass on the verified result.
- SCOPE: full COSMOS2 (cosmos/ core modules) + cDeck (builds/cdeck/ui/, src-tauri/), with explicit emphasis on cDeck's tabs and their functioning: studio, runs, orders, review, gitur, surfaces, recents, voice, system, models, backup, tools, clock, open, settings, forge, crucible, diligence, docket, ups, differentiator, website, and the Profiles popup.

- TABS FLAGGED AS LIKELY INCOMPLETE (verify against live tree, do not assume): forge, crucible, diligence, docket, ups, differentiator.
- THE BLUEPRINT IS NOT A DELIVERABLE CODEBASE. It is a non-authoritative planning roadmap: goal, current state, gap, proposed approach, risk notes, suggested job breakdown. It must NOT be formatted as a diff, must NOT be run through the local deterministic gate, must NOT get a CCr lease job or Gitur branch directly. Only AFTER Keith and/or Grok 4.6 review and explicitly approve specific pieces of the blueprint do those pieces become real CREW/OUT jobs against real live-slice bytes, through the normal pipeline.

# SECTION 2 — BINDING RULES FOR THIS PACKAGE SPECIFICALLY (CACHEABLE, DO NOT EDIT)

These rules govern execution of THIS package only and sit alongside Section 1 in the frozen prefix. They exist to prevent the four most likely execution mistakes: skipping the fix step, reviewing the wrong (stale) state on Day 2, treating the blueprint as authoritative, and silently spending the reserve.

**RULE A — SEQUENCE IS MANDATORY, NOT ADVISORY.**
Execute Section 4 queries in numeric order: 1, 2, 3, 5, 5b, then the crew-job gap (outside this file, using the existing pipeline), then 6, 7, 8, 9. Do not run Query 6 (Day 2 verification) before the crew-job gap has actually merged real fixes. Verifying pre-fix state twice is not "extra safety" — it is wasted spend that produces zero new information, explicitly forbidden by the budget note in Section 1 Session 4.

**RULE B — TWO DIFFERENT MODEL FAMILIES FOR EVERY REVIEW PAIR.**
Query 1 (Sol) and Query 2 (Fable 5.1) must run on different model families. Query 6 (Sol) and Query 7 (Fable 5.1) must also run on different model families. If Fable 5.1 is unavailable for any reason, substitute Terra — but do NOT substitute Sol for both slots in a pair under any circumstance.

**RULE C — TIE-BREAKER IS CONDITIONAL, NOT AUTOMATIC.**
Query 8 (Terra tie-breaker) fires ONLY if Query 1 and Query 2 (or Query 6 and Query 7) disagree on the COMPLETE/INCOMPLETE status of at least one tab, or disagree on a BLOCKING finding. If both reviewers agree on everything, skip Query 8 entirely and note "no disagreement, tie-breaker skipped" in the disposition log. Do not run it "just in case."

**RULE D — THE BLUEPRINT NEVER BYPASSES THE PIPELINE.**
Output from Query 5 (blueprint) and Query 5b (blueprint critique) gets written to the disposition log and presented to Keith / used by Grok 4.6 to draft NEW CREW/OUT job specs. It is never itself submitted as a job, never run through the local gate, never given a CCr lease, never opened as a Gitur PR. If you are about to do any of those four things with blueprint text directly, STOP — that is the exact mistake this rule exists to prevent.

**RULE E — RESERVE PROTECTION.**
Total spend through Query 8 should land near $5.71 (modeled). If actual spend exceeds $10 before reaching Query 8, STOP, do not proceed to remaining queries, and log the overage with a specific reason in the disposition log before asking Keith whether to continue. The ~$14 gap between $5.71 and $20 is contingency for genuine surprises (a severity Query 1/2 didn't anticipate, a failed call needing retry) — it is not a bigger budget for the same four-step plan.

**RULE F — DAY 2 REVIEWS THE POST-FIX STATE, EXPLICITLY.**
Query 6 and Query 7 must include, in their ITEM, the actual diffs/files that changed between Day 1 and Day 2 (i.e., the crew-job outputs that merged in the gap). If no crew jobs were approved or merged from the blueprint, Query 6/7 still run, but note in the ITEM that this is a re-confirmation of Day 1 state, not a post-fix check — and flag this explicitly in the disposition log, since it means the blueprint stage produced no actioned output, which is itself a finding worth surfacing to Keith.

END SECTION 2.
